subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept the exact-head native MXC dependency graph and upstream argv-carried sandbox envelope as a first-party Windows sandbox plugin boundary?
rationale: The known implementation defects have been repaired and the real behavior proof is strong, but automation cannot authorize native dependency execution or decide whether process-list exposure of the sandbox request is acceptable.

options.title: Approve with secops signoff
options.body: Accept the current dependency graph and preview argv transport after exact-head admin or secops review, then proceed through normal merge gates.

options.title: Wait for safer transport
options.body: Keep the PR open until the MXC SDK supports a file, stdin, pipe, or equivalent non-argv request transport.

options.title: Decline first-party ownership
options.body: Keep MXC independently distributed until OpenClaw is ready to own the native dependency and Windows support contract.

recommendation.title: Approve with secops signoff
recommendation.body: Accept the current dependency graph and preview argv transport after exact-head admin or secops review, then proceed through normal merge gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The live PR assigns this security-sensitive product and dependency decision to steipete.
